A stronger claim of clean certification is not well supported because the policy text says certification without material caveats requires either no current material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, and the admissible record shows that standard is not met. That reframing is useful, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate. The distinction matters: a caveated position can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat is already implemented or otherwise satisfied in the evidentiary record. On that basis, certification may be plausible in principle if disclosure or approved acceptance is completed before launch, but current compliance is not evidenced.
